questions.question: When loading a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put a balanced amount of weight over the axles.
Do not worry about how weight is distributed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put a balanced amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly balanced. Too much weight over an axle can damage it and make steering harder. Too little weight can cause poor traction and bad handling.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is usually:
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable. The meat swings around while the truck moves, and its center of gravity is high.

questions.question: A high center of gravity when loading cargo:

options.text: Increases the chance of a rollover.
Increases the chance that items will fall down.
Makes unloading the cargo more difficult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the chance of a rollover.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity increases the risk that the vehicle will tip over. Load cargo with proper weight distribution.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo

questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: Brakes that are out of adjustment will:

options.text: Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes will wear out faster than properly adjusted ones. Check brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: Some air brake systems add alcohol to:

options.text: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
Prevent people from breathing air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to stop ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: During the driving test at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: When approaching a drawbridge with a green traffic light:

options.text: You must wait for the light to change to yellow.

questions.explanation: If a drawbridge has a green traffic light, you do not need to stop. However, always slow down before crossing a drawbridge to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil buildup. This buildup can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Improper cargo loading:
questions.explanation: Proper cargo loading is essential for safety. Improperly loaded cargo can damage the vehicle or fall off during a crash or sudden stop, causing injury or death.

questions.question: What skill must you show on a basic vehicle control test?
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test includes straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Friction in an S-cam brake happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: If you transport hazardous materials that need placards, you must:

options.text: Ask permission from local law enforcement.
Transport the materials only at night.

questions.explanation: To drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials requiring placards, you must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: The air compressor is connected to the:
questions.explanation: The air compressor is connected to the engine through gears or a belt. It can be cooled by air or by the engine cooling system.

questions.question: If you use spring brakes with a heavy load, stopping will:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. When spring brakes activate due to low air pressure, your vehicle needs more distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: While driving with passengers, a bus driver should:

options.text: Talk with passengers if they start the conversation.

questions.explanation: A bus driver is responsible for passenger safety. To stay focused and reduce driving dangers, a bus driver should not talk with passengers while driving.

questions.question: The standee line:

options.text: Is a line passengers should not cross.
Is a line where passengers should stand.
Is a line passengers use when leaving the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a line passengers should not cross.
questions.explanation: On a bus with standing room, passengers cannot stand in front of the driver's seat. Buses must have a line or mark on the floor to show where passengers cannot stand. This is called a standee line.

questions.question: Manual air tank drains should be:

options.text: Opened daily to drain the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opened daily to drain the tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems contains water and compressor oil. This buildup can damage the brakes. You must open manual air tank drains daily to remove water and oil.

questions.question: After a bus trip ends, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be returned without an inspection.

questions.explanation: Inspect every bus at the end of each trip. Passengers may have damaged safety items. Inspections catch these problems so they can be fixed before the next trip.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, it is important to:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible on the axles.
Put the right amount of weight on the axles.
Not worry about how cargo weight is spread out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight on the axles.
questions.explanation: When loading cargo, each axle must have the right amount of weight—not too little and not too much. Wrong loading can make steering difficult, reduce tire grip, or damage the axles.
